lines.text: You're the overnight guest. It's two fifty-eight in the morning. The storm just stopped.
lines.beat_before: hook: the phone camera in the bedroom in a roaring storm, lightning through the French doors; the storm cuts to dead silence and the rain stops in the air

lines.text: Monte Cristo Homestead. Junee, New South Wales. Built in the eighteen eighties by the Crawley family.
lines.beat_before: cut to the house from outside, wet, moonlit; our window lit upstairs

lines.text: Mister Crawley died here in nineteen ten. His wife stayed on, and rarely left the house again.
lines.beat_before: cut to the upstairs hall from your door: candlelight under the far door

lines.text: For decades, guests who spent the night have reported footsteps on the balcony. Voices. Being touched.
lines.beat_before: the candlelight under the door goes out; cut back to the room

lines.text: No one has ever proven anything. The house closed to visitors in twenty twenty-five.
lines.beat_before: the phone light sweeps the room; the wardrobe door creaks open by itself

lines.text: You hear the footsteps now. On the balcony, outside your door.
lines.beat_before: the phone turns to the French doors
behind the lace, a woman in black walks past on the balcony, and stops at the doors
